_note: The Story of Prophet Dhu al-Kifl, drawn strictly from the Qur'an (Surahs al-Anbiya and Sad). The Qur'an names Dhu al-Kifl twice — among the patient whom Allah admitted into His mercy, and among the outstanding and righteous — but relates no narrative, and the scholars differ over his identity. This chronicle says only what the text says and claims no more. No figural imagery; summaries carry no Arabic script.

events.title: Among the Patient
events.summary: 'And Ismail and Idris and Dhul-Kifl — all were of the patient. And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were of the righteous.' The Qur'an sets Dhu al-Kifl beside Ismail and Idris under a single praise: patience, mercy received, and righteousness — the honour of a name, without a story attached.
events.why: What the Qur'an chooses to preserve about Dhu al-Kifl is not an event but a quality — ṣabr, patience — and its reward: entry into Allah's mercy. The lesson is the character, not the chronicle.

media.caption: Calligraphic panel — “All were of the patient” (al-Anbiya 21:85).

events.title: Among the Outstanding
events.summary: 'And remember Ismail, al-Yasaʿ, and Dhul-Kifl, and all are among the outstanding.' A second time the Qur'an names Dhu al-Kifl among the chosen and the best of servants — and a second time it relates nothing of his life, leaving his identity and story among the things known only to Allah.
events.why: The Qur'an's restraint is itself the teaching: it grants Dhu al-Kifl the highest company and the highest praise, and withholds the rest — a reminder to honour him as Allah did, and to add nothing of our own.

media.caption: Calligraphic panel — “All are among the outstanding” (Sad 38:48).

paths.title: The Arc of Dhu al-Kifl
paths.blurb: All the Qur'an says of Dhu al-Kifl — twice named among the chosen: of the patient admitted into Allah's mercy, and among the outstanding.
